_README: Agronomic thresholds used by the UbiMap suitability and rotation models. Every threshold carries the source it came from. Nothing in here is invented: values marked verified=false are the team's working values and must be confirmed against the cited source before the project is published. scripts/check_sources.py prints the audit table.

annual_rainfall_mm.source: DA Regional Field Office 02, Ubi Production Guide (Nov 2012), pp. 6-7: at least 130 cm annual rainfall is needed. FAO EcoCrop Dioscorea alata id 936: optimal 1,200 to 4,000 mm, absolute 700 to 8,000 mm.

monthly_rainfall_mm.source: Team working band, derived from the 1,000 to 1,500 mm over 6 to 7 months figure in CABI Compendium, Dioscorea alata. NOT VERIFIED as a monthly figure in any Philippine source.

air_temp_c.source: DA RFO 02 pp. 6-7: optimum temperatures range from 25 to 30 degrees C. FAO EcoCrop id 936 gives 20 to 32 optimal and a 40 degree absolute ceiling. The 32 degree heat stress figure is a TEAM ESTIMATE: no Philippine source states a heat stress threshold.

soil_ph.source: FAO EcoCrop Dioscorea alata id 936, fetched live 15 Nov 2026: pH 5.5 to 6.5 optimal, 4.8 to 8.5 absolute. The Pagadian site itself measures pH 5.36 to 5.49 in SoilGrids, so it sits inside the optimal band.

slope_deg.source: TEAM ESTIMATE. No Philippine source states a slope limit for ube. The basis is that the crop is a tuber with exposed ridges and that the DA guide describes medium and low elevation areas. NOT VERIFIED.

soil_depth_cm.note: EcoCrop gives deep, over 150 cm, as optimal and 50 to 150 cm as absolute. The crop needs a deep soil for the tuber.

root_zone_wetness_index.note: NASA POWER GWETROOT is a dimensionless MERRA-2 root zone wetness index from 0 to 1, not m3/m3. It is used only to sharpen the rainfall driven waterlogging signal, never as an absolute threshold.
root_zone_wetness_index.source: NASA POWER parameter definition, MERRA-2 Root Zone Soil Wetness (1)

waterlogging_monthly_rain_mm.note: A month with at least this much rain is a heavy rain month. Sustained heavy rain in the tuber bulking stage is the main rot risk for ube. The 250 mm figure is the PAGASA wet season threshold.
waterlogging_monthly_rain_mm.source: PAGASA climate classification, 250 mm over three consecutive months

drought_monthly_rain_mm.note: A month with less than this much rain is a dry month. PAGASA dry season threshold.
drought_monthly_rain_mm.source: PAGASA climate classification, 50 mm over three consecutive months

planting_stress_monthly_rain_mm.note: A month under this much rain is a shoulder month in PAGASA terms, and is the risky stretch for planting and establishment.
planting_stress_monthly_rain_mm.source: PAGASA monthly wet season threshold of 100 mm

dry_season_requirement.note: Ube needs a dry maturation window. The DA guide plants in March to May and harvests from late November to February, so the tuber bulks and cures in the dry season. A field that is wet in every month of the year cannot do this. The first version of this model scored rainfall amount only, and validation against PSA production data showed it could not tell a real ube province from a non producing one. Adding this requirement is what fixed it. The number of months under 50 mm of rain is the observable with the strongest measured relationship to real provincial yield, r = +0.36 for NASA POWER and r = +0.30 for GPM IMERG over 17 provinces. The signal is positive but modest, because yield also depends on things no satellite sees.
dry_season_requirement.source: Team requirement derived from the DA RFO 02 planting and harvest windows, then confirmed by the PSA validation run in data/validation_results.json

duration_months.source: DA RFO 02 pp. 14-15: around 10 to 11 months from planting to harvest, with early harvest possible at 6 to 7 months.

planting_window.note: DA RFO 02 pp. 8-9: usually planted from March to May, best at the start of the rainy season. ATI-7 gives early planting in April.
planting_window.source: DA RFO 02 Ubi Production Guide pp. 8-9; ATI-7

harvest_window.note: DA RFO 02 pp. 14-15: harvesting is usually done from late November to February of the following year.
harvest_window.source: DA RFO 02 Ubi Production Guide pp. 14-15; USDA FAS RP2026-0019 p. 2

yield_t_ha.source: DA RFO 02 Cost and Return Analysis pp. 16-17 gives 30 and 20 t/ha; the achieved figures are computed from PSA OpenSTAT 2025.

clay_percent.note: FAO EcoCrop gives medium and light textures as preferred. The DA guide says clay loam with high organic matter is preferred, but it also requires a well-drained area, so heavy clay is a risk rather than a virtue. Team working value.
clay_percent.source: FAO EcoCrop id 936, texture 'medium, light'; DA RFO 02 pp. 6-7

price_php_per_kg.source: DA RFO 02 pp. 16-17, 2012 guide prices. 2025 market prices were not re-verified in this pass.

traits.notes: Ube does not fix nitrogen. It is a monocot in Dioscoreaceae with no rhizobial symbiosis, and a hectare yielding 35 t removes about 128 kg N, 39 kg P2O5 and 195 kg K2O. Waterlogging is not tolerated at all: the DA guide requires a well-drained area, because the tuber rots in standing water. The same-family rule is a yam-to-yam rule, not a Philippine published rule: the anthracnose pathogen Colletotrichum gloeosporioides infects many crops and weeds and survives on crop debris, so a yam crop after a yam crop is the risk. The IPPC advice for yam anthracnose names maize barrier crops, crop rotation, and ploughing in residues immediately after harvest; ATI-7 lists a cropping system with legumes.

risks.mitigation_en: Plant on a ridge or raised bed and clear drainage ditches before the peak of the rains. The crop does not tolerate standing water at all.
risks.mitigation_bis: Tabon og gamay nga alima, ug himoon ang dugo sa dili pa mahumug ang ulan. Dili gyawan sa ube ang tuyob nga tubig.

risks.text_en: Anthracnose, the most limiting disease of ube
risks.text_bis: Anthracnose, ang labing hadlok nga sakit sa ube
risks.mitigation_en: Use clean planting material, avoid overhead watering late in the day, plough crop residues in immediately after harvest, and confirm a spray programme with your municipal agriculturist.
risks.mitigation_bis: Gamit nga limpyong material sa pagtani, ayaw i-water sa gab-i, i-plow ang mga basag sa umang abot dayon, ug kumpirma ang spray plan sa imong lokal na agronomista.

risks.text_en: Root knot nematode and tuber rot carry over
risks.text_bis: Nematode ug kadaot sa tubero nga naa labaw
risks.mitigation_en: Do not follow ube with another yam on the same plot. Rotate with a non-yam crop and plough the residues in.
risks.mitigation_bis: Ayaw i-follow ang ube og lain nga yam sa samang luna. Palit og tanom nga dili yam, ug i-plow ang basag.

mungbean.why: Fixes nitrogen, short cycle, uses the dry season after ube harvest.

peanut.why: Fixes nitrogen, tolerates a dry season, adds a marketable harvest.

sweetpotato.why: Keeps soil covered and breaks the ube pest cycle because it is a different plant family.

corn.why: The common upland crop in the pilot area. Heavy nitrogen feeder, and bare soil between seasons.

cassava.why: Drought tolerant and low input, but repeated cassava strips the soil and leaves it bare.

coconut.why: Perennial canopy that shades the ube vines, protects the soil from rain impact and keeps a crop income flowing.

rotation_library.why_en: This is your existing rotation. We compare every other option against it so you can see what actually changes.
rotation_library.why_bis: Kini ang imong kasamtanan karon. Gitawag nato ang tanan nga opsyon labaw niini aron makita nimo unsay gyud naayo.
benefits_en: No change in cost or routine
You already know the market and the buyers
gaps_en: Bare soil between seasons lets the topsoil wash away
Same crop every year drains nitrogen
risks_en: Repeated cropping of the same plant family keeps pest pressure high
Nitrogen falls every season without a legume to fix it

rotation_library.why_en: Ube takes the rainy season, when your field already has reliable rain, and the legume takes the dry season and puts nitrogen back.
rotation_library.why_bis: Ube ang una sa panahon sa ulan, kung regular nga ulan, ang legume dayon sa panahon sa katag aron mabalik og nitrogen sa yuta.
benefits_en: Two marketable harvests in one year
The legume fixes nitrogen the ube took
Different plant families, so the ube pest cycle breaks
gaps_en: No field-level soil pH for your plot yet
Ube planting material is the real bottleneck. The Department of Agriculture suspended fresh tuber exports in September 2026 to protect seed stocks, so setts are scarce and dear
Anthracnose pressure cannot be predicted from satellite data
risks_en: Waterlogging in the peak rains can rot the tubers. Ube does not tolerate standing water at all
Anthracnose is the most limiting disease of ube and survives on crop debris, so plough the residues in
benefits_bis: Duha ka marketable nga ani sa usa ka tuig
Ang legume ang mabalik og nitrogen sa yuta
Lain nga pamilya sa tanom, maa mapahili ang peste sa ube

rotation_library.name_en: Ube under coconut, with a legume cover
rotation_library.name_bis: Ube ilaw sa niyo, dayon legume nga cover
rotation_library.name_fil: Ube sa ilalim ng niyo, may legume na cover
rotation_library.why_en: If your farm has coconut, the ube vines climb the palms and use the shade. The palm keeps the soil covered and the legume between palms adds nitrogen.
rotation_library.why_bis: Kon may niyo ang imong uma, ang mga ube nga uyab sa palayot ug saka, gamit ang anino. Ang niyo nagpugong sa yuta, ang legume nga naa tali-tali sa palayot makatabang og nitrogen.
benefits_en: Coconut income continues while the ube establishes
Permanent soil cover protects the slope
Lower cost because you already own the land and the palms
gaps_en: We need a field visit to confirm palm density and shade level
Mechanisation is difficult between the palms
risks_en: Too much shade lowers tuber size
Coconut and ube compete for water during a dry spell
benefits_bis: Padili ang kita sa niyo samtang gikaabot ang ube
Perminente nga cover nga nagpugong sa yuta
Mas mura tungod sa imong gipukong na yuta ug mga palayot

rotation_library.name_en: Ube, sweet potato, then a legume
rotation_library.why_en: Three different plant families in three seasons. Sweet potato keeps the ground covered after the ube is lifted and feeds the livestock.
rotation_library.why_bis: Tatlong lain nga pamilya sa tanom sa tulo ka panahon. Ang kamote nagpugong sa yuta human ma-ani ang ube, ug naa usab nga ammo sa hayop.
benefits_en: Strongest pest cycle break because no family repeats
Almost no bare soil through the year
Sweet potato vines are good fodder
gaps_en: Three crops means more labour and more risk of a mistake
Sweet potato market price is not tracked in this build
risks_en: More complex, so it needs more careful scheduling
If the ube harvest slips, the sweet potato planting window is squeezed
benefits_bis: Kusog nga pagbasak sa siklo sa peste kay walay pamilya nga naaulit
Walay hubad nga yuta sa tibuk nga tuig
Ang mga tanom sa kamote maayo nga ammo sa hayop
